analysis.title: The rock we all stood on is shaking
key_insights: Q3 2026 earnings growth remains strong but is no longer accelerating, per Goldman's David Kostin, ending the pattern of acceleration seen over the last few quarters.
Median S&P 500 company revenue growth slowed from 7.4% in Q1 to 7.2% in Q2 and 7.0% in Q3 (FactSet). Consensus expects 6.4% in Q4.
Companies are still beating EPS estimates, but Q3 cumulative EPS surprise is running well below the levels seen in Q1 and Q2 (GIR).
Jefferies finds revenue guidance revisions for C26 are much less positive on balance, while EPS revisions remain strong. Bottom line is holding up better than the top line.
Earnings beats are generating little price reaction while misses are punished aggressively, particularly in large-cap tech (Jefferies).
Jefferies argues the weakness is in outlooks rather than reported numbers. Cautious guidance is weighing on sentiment, and the SPX is back to 18.4x NTM EPS.

Goldman's Tony Pasquariello says Q3 will be remembered as a disappointment: a few cloud businesses are compounding huge growth, but several large players missed in the core of their business while hyperscaler capex intentions are not slowing.

sector_views.rationale: Misses are punished aggressively in large-cap tech, and several big players missed in their core businesses despite strong growth in some cloud units.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 S&P 500 earnings growth is strong but no longer accelerating (Goldman, Kostin).
Median S&P 500 revenue growth: 7.4% in Q1, 7.2% in Q2, 7.0% in Q3 (reported, FactSet). Q4 consensus estimate is 6.4%.
Q3 cumulative EPS surprise is below Q1 and Q2 levels (GIR). Companies are still beating, by smaller margins.
Jefferies: C26 revenue guidance revisions are much less positive while EPS revisions remain strong.
Beats draw little reaction and misses are punished, especially in large-cap tech (Jefferies).
Goldman's Pasquariello: several large hyperscalers missed in the core of their business in Q3 while a few cloud businesses compound huge growth.
risk_factors: Slowing revenue growth, with a consensus Q4 median of 6.4%.
Weaker revenue guidance for C26 even as EPS revisions hold up.
Aggressive punishment of misses in large-cap tech.
Hyperscaler capex not slowing while returns, capital and free cash flow remain debated.
vol_and_positioning: SPX is trading at 18.4x NTM EPS (Jefferies), described as back down.
Asymmetric price reaction to earnings: little upside reaction to beats, aggressive downside reaction to misses in large-cap tech.
